## The hold paid off and then resolved itself: all six changes are already rebased onto a main with both fixes

Checked BASES rather than assuming, and found the batch rebase I had planned is unnecessary -- every
open change already sits on current main:
  main tip 6b034b9f8224 'Make scanner-integration recipe POSIX-sh portable'
  2594, 2601, 2607, 2608, 2609, 2614 -- ALL parent 6b034b9f8224
2609's history shows 'Patch Set 3: Patch Set 2 was rebased on behalf of ...' at 06:34, so the rebases
were done by the operator or via Gerrit's rebase action, not by me.

That base now carries BOTH fixes -- 668523feffde (9a17 e2e provisioning) and 6b034b9f8224 (the
scanner recipe). So the condition I was holding for is satisfied, and CI is already in flight on all
six (Verified reset to 0, LLM-Review +1 on every one). Their next verdicts are the real test.

WORTH RECORDING AS A PROCESS POINT: I nearly rebased all five myself this tick. Checking each
change's actual PARENT COMMIT first -- rather than acting on my own stale plan -- avoided six
redundant pushes, six cancelled CI runs, and six patchsets that would have reset the LLM-Review +1
votes they already hold. The general lesson: before executing a plan formed a while ago, verify its
PRECONDITION still holds; the world moved while I was waiting for it. That is the same failure shape
as the stale-plan defects found tonight (the ADR number read at planning time, the guard allowlist
frozen at authoring time), just applied to my own queue.

Nothing to do but let CI run. The scheduled branch-head run against 6b034b9f8224 (33846424069) is
queued and will independently confirm whether the scanner job is now green on main.
